Doctoral Degrees
PhD in Intelligent Systems
Students in this program will gain an advanced knowledge in intelligent systems through interdisciplinary research and collaboration across other schools at the University of Pittsburgh. Students will explore artificial intelligence and how it relates to other disciplines like computer science, medicine, psychology, education, law, and more.
The GRE is optional for admission to this program.
At A Glance
Credits: 72 Duration: 5+ years to complete Format: On campus
Application Deadline: January 15 (Fall term) Next Start Date: August 23, 2027
Tuition Apply Now
Admissions Requirements
General guidelines for applying to a graduate program at the University of Pittsburgh should be reviewed prior to submitting an application for admission. These guidelines are available on the University’s Application for Admission Catalog page.
All applicants will be judged on their own merits. Applicants for master’s study must have earned a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a scholastic average of B (3.0 on a 4.0 scale) or better; the doctoral programs have more stringent requirements. For those who have been in the workforce, admission will be based upon academic achievement, area of study, career orientation and work experience.
PhD in Intelligent Systems Admissions Requirements
Briefly, an application consists of the standard SCI admission form and supplemental materials. Applicants must also include a concise statement of purpose, providing information on the following points:
Objective in pursuing a PhD or MS in intelligent systems.
Theoretical background in relevant areas.
Background in relevant tools and applications, particularly programming languages, including the level of proficiency.
Relevant practical experience,including industrial or commercial experience.
Applicants to the Biomedical Informatics track of the Intelligent Systems Program must specifically indicate their interest in this track on their application to the Intelligent Systems Program.
Coursework
This program requires a minimum of 72 credits. Students have a choice between the general intelligent systems track and the biomedical informatics track. Students typically complete this program in five to seven years, depending on their full-time or part-time status and how quickly program milestones are met. View full PhD in Intelligent Systems degree requirements in the Pitt Course Catalog.
